Use `snl library html` to render one validated Library as HTML for inspection or publication staging.

### Availability
This Entry is a normative product contract. The command is implemented only when its canonical path appears in machine-readable `snl --help`; absence means planned and unavailable, never silently emulated through a different command.


### Command path
`library/html` is the canonical transport-neutral command. The intended shell spelling is `snl library html`. Current availability is advertised by machine-readable `snl --help`; an Agent/MCP adapter submits the same operation object instead of reconstructing shell text.

### Operation request
```json
{"protocol":"snl.operation/v1","command":"library/html","root":"/absolute/workspace","arguments":{"id":"<library-slug>","language":null}}
```
Every adapter accepts exactly this semantic request. Unknown argument keys are rejected. The CLI accepts `--root` and `--json` globally and emits one complete JSON document followed by a newline. Rendering uses current canonical entities and fails closed on unresolved topology/content. Under `--json`, HTML is returned inside `data.artifact`; shell `--output <file>` is adapter-only, writes atomically, and `--output -` is rejected.

### Success result
A successful call exits `0` and returns `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":true,"command":"library/html","data":{},"diagnostics":[]}`. `data.artifact` contains deterministic standalone HTML with media type, encoding, digest, and diagnostics; with shell `--output <file>`, `data` instead identifies the atomically published path and digest.

### Failure and exit semantics
Domain rejection (invalid data, not-found, conflict, or validation errors) exits `1`. Invocation, input I/O, unsupported workspace/schema, lock acquisition, and runtime failures exit `2`. Failure stdout under `--json` is exactly one `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":false,"command":"library/html","error":{"code":"<stable-code>","message":"<actionable text>","details":{},"retryable":false}}`; no stack trace or prose contaminates stdout.

### State and concurrency
Read-only with respect to workspace; explicit output publication is atomic. Revisions, cursors, checked digests, and workspace revisions are opaque tokens. Repeated calls against unchanged bytes return equivalent semantic results.
